transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I keep misplacing order tickets and other important things at the shop, and it’s starting to hurt my business. Since I took over running my own dry cleaning boutique two years ago, I've been really overwhelmed trying to keep track of everything. A friend from my church noticed how much I was struggling and suggested I come in to get evaluated.
Did these problems with organization, forgetfulness, and feeling overwhelmed exist before you took over the shop or start only after the job change or another stressful event?

They've definitely gotten much worse since I took over the shop, but I've actually had milder versions of these issues my whole life. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was always chatting, getting out of my seat, and losing my worksheets or homework.
Did you have similar problems with inattention, restlessness, or being overly active before age 12, in more than one setting like school and home?

Yes, it was definitely happening in both places before I was 12. At school, my teachers were always writing notes about me chatting and losing my schoolwork, and at home, my parents constantly scolded me for losing my shoes or refusing to sit still at the dinner table.
Do these attention, forgetfulness, and restlessness problems still happen in your current daily life now, and do they cause problems in more than one area such as work, home, or relationships?

Yes, they definitely affect me every day now across my work, home, and church life. At the shop, I'm staying late several nights a week to fix mistakes and have had some very upset customers, while at home, my husband complains I'm too drained and distracted to be present. It has also really strained my energy for my church commitments, which used to be so important to me.
Do you also have trouble with impulsive behaviors, like interrupting others, blurting out answers, or acting before thinking?

Yes, I definitely do. I often jump in and blurt out answers or finish people's sentences before they're done talking, which sometimes backfires because I didn't actually listen to the whole thing. I also catch myself interrupting conversations at church or hovering over my employees at the shop to comment on their work without being asked.
Do you also have trouble sitting still or feeling physically restless, like fidgeting, leaving your seat, or feeling driven to keep moving, even when you need to stay seated?

Yes, I really struggle with that and feel very restless. During long meetings at church or when I try to do computer work at the shop, I keep popping up from my chair to straighten a rack, check the front door, or get a drink. I just feel too fidgety to sit still for very long.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a lifelong pattern beginning before age 12, present in both school and home settings, with persistent inattention/disorganization, forgetfulness, hyperactivity/restlessness, and impulsive interrupting. Symptoms are currently impairing work, home, and church functioning, consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive with hyperactive-impulsive symptoms; however, the provided candidate list only includes F90.0 and the presentation fits ADHD/attention-deficit disorder.
